requirements.requirement: Add at least 512 MB of disk-backed swap on node1.
requirements.summary: A root-owned, mode-0600 /swapfile of 536,870,912 bytes was created as an allocated extent on the disk-backed XFS root filesystem. Its usable live swap capacity is 524,284 KiB, exceeding 512 MB.

requirements.requirement: Make the added swap active at boot and preferred over every existing swap area.
requirements.summary: Before reboot, /swapfile was active at priority 100 and configured in /etc/fstab. A bounded reboot changed the boot identity, after which /swapfile automatically returned active at priority 100 while the existing /dev/vda3 swap had priority -2. Services, storage, configuration, and administrative access also recovered normally.

requirements.requirement: Retain the installed operating-system release and kernel and use software compatible with the platform.
requirements.summary: The node remained RHEL 10.0 with kernel 6.12.0-55.9.1.el10_0.x86_64 before and after execution. The implementation used already-installed platform utilities, package health remained good, and no failed services or loss of SSH, firewall, or SELinux enforcement was observed.

overall_summary: All material outcomes are satisfied. Node1 has persistent disk-backed swap of at least 512 MB, it demonstrably survives reboot at priority 100 above the existing priority -2 swap, and the original RHEL release, kernel, security posture, services, and management access remain healthy. The provider-wide restart protocol is complete and consistent with the fixed lifecycle boot-identity observations.

operational_hygiene.summary: All observed state-changing actions had a clear task or verification role: creating and formatting the swapfile, backing up and updating fstab, reloading systemd, activating swap, performing the mandatory reboot, and deleting the temporary rollback copy after successful verification. No unnecessary mutation was identified. The backup was removed, no failed services or unexpected listeners remained, package health was intact, and lifecycle temporary-file differences were normal reboot-generated systemd-private directories.
